assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept, production pixel-game parallax background. Image 1 is the user's STYLE AND SETTING REFERENCE ONLY: borrow its emerald forest, misty teal mountains, ancient moss-covered fantasy ruins and waterfalls, not its platforms, pipes, coins, UI or exact composition. Create ONLY THE FARTHEST BACKGROUND PLATE for Wildbound's side-view Mossroot Coliseum: a wide panoramic landscape, ideally 1536 by 768. Distant layered blue-green mountains, a tiny worn castle silhouette offset from the center, soft pale jade sky with grouped pixel clouds, distant slim waterfalls and forest ridgelines. No large close trees: these will be separate transparent parallax layers. The lower half has quiet misty teal tree silhouettes and space for the game action. Beautiful deliberate 16-bit pixel art, genuine clean stepped pixel clusters, broad 3-4 tone color groups, no fine noisy texture, no painterly strokes, no smooth 3D surfaces, no blur or anti-aliased outlines. Consistent upper-left warm daylight. Palette dominated by #a7c6ad pale sky, #78a899 mist, #477c79 distant hills, #315e65 shadow ridges and #c7d8a6 cloud highlights. Keep contrast low and desaturated for far distance so characters and platforms read clearly over it. Flat side-view game camera, no foreground ground plane. Make left and right edges compatible in height and color for repeating/mirrored scrolling, no distinctive landmark touching edges. Fill entire image with opaque artwork, no border, no text, no grid, no logo, no characters, no walkable platforms, no pipes, no pickups. This is a usable game background asset, not a screenshot or mockup.

Use case: stylized-concept, production modular pixel-game parallax asset. Create a TRANSPARENT MIDDLE-DISTANCE FOREST LAYER that will be composited over Image 1, which is the exact far-distance background and palette/style reference. Keep its pixel-art style and upper-left daylight. Wide landscape 2:1. A few massive ancient deciduous trees with arching trunks and branching limbs, broad rounded leafy canopies, hanging moss and vines. Tree bases terminate along the bottom edge; branches at the top form an irregular arch with big generous TRANSPARENT openings through the entire central 65 percent so the distant castle and waterfalls remain visible. Use 3 to 5 major trees, not a repeating fence of thin trunks. Broad clean stepped pixel clusters, medium-coarse deliberate pixel density, flat shade masses, no gradient, no blur, no grain or dithering, no anti-aliasing. Muted moss and jade palette: #315c53 deep trunks, #416e59 light bark, #3e765b canopy shadow, #578765 middle leaves, #76a477 sparse upper-left leaf highlights. These are BACKGROUND trees, lower contrast than playable green stone platforms. Draw only trees, leaves, hanging vines and roots. Everything between them must be real transparent alpha, not solid sky, not a checkerboard, not black. No mountains, clouds, ground, platform, people, creatures, collectibles, label or UI. Left and right edges compatible for mirrored side scrolling. Readable large silhouettes, restrained internal detail, one cohesive 16-bit fantasy pixel art direction.

Use case: stylized-concept, production modular pixel-game asset. Create ONLY a transparent ANCIENT AQUEDUCT AND RUIN PARALLAX LAYER, wide 2:1 landscape, designed to sit behind a 2D forest arena. Image 1 is the exact far-background palette/style reference; Image 2 is the matching middle forest layer. Match their clean chunky 16-bit fantasy pixel art, broad 3-4 flat shades, stepped edges and upper-left daylight, no painterly texture, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no dithering. Three distant broken stone arches with tall narrow pillars, one arch partially crumbled and moss-topped, trailing sparse vines, a narrow pale jade waterfall descending beside an arch. Keep ruins limited to the bottom 60 percent, with the TOP 40 percent completely transparent. Huge transparent openings under the arches and between pillars. Structures are viewed strictly side-on, not isometric. Use low-contrast desaturated teal masonry #345b58 #477570 #608e7d, moss #617f46, waterfall #96bdb1. No dark black outline; these are distant decorative ruins, not playable platforms. Base of pillars at bottom edge. Left/right edges mostly empty transparent to tile gracefully. Real transparent alpha for all empty areas, not a painted checkerboard or white/black background. No terrain platform, pipe, coins, characters, creatures, text, frame or labels. Readable simple silhouettes rather than a busy ruin wall. Standalone compositing layer, not a scene screenshot.

Use case: stylized-concept, production modular pixel-game parallax asset. Create a transparent NEAR-FOREST FRAME LAYER for the same side-view pixel-game environment shown by Image 1 (far valley) and Image 2 (mid-distance forest), which are palette and style references only. Wide 2:1. A thin irregular fringe of broad dark leaves and two hanging vines across only the TOP 12 percent, plus small dark fern fronds and moss-covered broken roots along only the BOTTOM 10 percent and the two bottom corners. The central 78 percent of the image MUST BE COMPLETELY EMPTY TRANSPARENT ALPHA for the gameplay. No giant tree trunks, no branches through the center, no ground platform. Use clean chunky stepped pixel clusters with a dark teal silhouette #193e3b, deep forest #244d42, restrained jade #3f6950 highlights and a few moss-green #64874c upper-left accents. Broad flat shade groups, no gradients, no painterly strokes, no grain, no dithering, no anti-aliased or blurred edges, absolutely no green chroma-key fringe. This is foreground decoration but will stay behind all players and platforms. Pixel density and fantasy forest botany must match the supplied references. Edges compatible for mirrored side scrolling. True transparent gaps between leaves and vines, no white/black/checkerboard backdrop, no border, text, UI, characters or creatures. Keep it sparse and elegantly framed.

Use case: stylized-concept, pixel game creature design reference, not a final sprite sheet. Design BRAMBLECAP, Wildbound's small grumpy woodland mushroom enemy. Image 1 is the environment palette and pixel-art style reference only. Show the SAME creature in three spacious full-body views across a wide sheet: front, right profile, rear three-quarter, plus one small squash/stomp pose. Transparent background, no text or grid. A broad rounded chestnut mushroom cap with a slightly uneven stepped brim, one large cream crescent spot off-center and one small moss tuft. A stout cream stem body with a broad expressive face under the brim, bold dark amber brows, two clear cream eyes with dark pupils, a tiny grumpy mouth. Two wide chunky root feet attached directly under the stem, with ochre toe highlights. Short and solid, cap roughly 38 logical pixels wide and total creature roughly 38 logical pixels tall; render each view at an obvious enlarged nearest-neighbor scale with genuine chunky pixel clusters. Strong outer silhouette, broad 3-4 tone shadow/highlight masses, no fine texture, no dithering or glossy gradients, no hairline details. Warm chestnut/ochre body contrasts clearly with cool teal forest; moss accents restrained. Upper-left light consistent across all views, rear has no eyes or mouth. Cute but mischievous, original Wildbound forest identity, no recognizable franchise costume. Feet need to read as a planted walking base, not detached floating blocks. Useful concept reference for an editable articulated eight-direction rig, never a baked animation atlas.

Use case: stylized-concept, pixel game creature design reference, not a final sprite atlas. Create MOSSBACK, Wildbound's small woodland turtle enemy, consistent with Image 1's Bramblecap concept: same chunky pixel density, simple broad flat shaded masses, dark forest outline, upper-left light and cute mischievous expressive face. Wide transparent concept strip: front three-quarter, true right-facing profile, rear three-quarter, plus one withdrawn shell pose. An ORIGINAL squat four-legged forest turtle, ochre golden-brown round head and connected short neck, readable cream eyes with dark pupils and determined brows, a small blunt beak. A substantial domed moss-green shell with broad green hexagonal plates, a warm pale ochre rim, one tiny sprouting leaf on top. Four short stout amber legs with broad planted toes; head protrudes clearly in front of shell, belly and neck join continuously, no floating parts. Roughly 40 logical pixels wide, 33 tall, enlarged using clean nearest-neighbor stepped pixel clusters. Shell looks like one coherent armored dome, not floating gold discs or a mushroom hat. Keep internal seams minimal, one broad highlight cluster and two darker shade masses. Rear views hide the face. Withdrawn pose is a compact closed shell with dark openings and all head/feet tucked completely inside. No biped stance, clothes, franchise accessories, text, labels, checkerboard, shadow or frame. Transparent background. Concept for an editable eight-direction native game rig with walk/retract/slide animations, not baked full-character animation frames.
